'''Peter James Lorimer''' (16 April 1939 – 7 February 2010) was a New Zealand mathematician. His research concerned [[group theory]], [[combinatorics]], and [[Ramsey theory]].

==Academic career==
Born in [[Christchurch]], Lorimer did a  [[BSc]] / [[MSc]] in mathematics at the [[University of Auckland]]  and won a [[Commonwealth Scholarship]] to do a [[PhD]] at [[McGill University]] in [[Montreal]], which he completed in 1963 under the supervision of [[Hans Schwerdtfeger]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=143236}}</ref> He returned to New Zealand to lecture, first at [[University of Canterbury]] and then at [[University of Auckland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/wiki/In_memoriam:_Peter_James_Lorimer_%2816.04.1939_-_7.02.2010%29 |title=In memoriam: Peter James Lorimer (16.04.1939 – 7.02.2010) – MathsDept |publisher=Math.auckland.ac.nz |date= |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/obituaries/peter-james-lorimer/ |title=Peter James Lorimer « Obituaries « Fellowship « The Academy « Our Organisation « Royal Society of New Zealand |publisher=Royalsociety.org.nz |date= |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>
